description: This topic covers the main circuit board of a computer, its various connectors, and the electronic pathways used for data transmission. It is a highly crucial and scoring section of Computer Knowledge for competitive exams.

sections.title: Motherboard and Bus Architecture
sections.description: The concept of communication pathways for data and signals between internal computer components.

key_concepts.explanation: The main Printed Circuit Board (PCB) of a computer that connects the CPU, memory, and all other hardware components. It is also known as the Logic Board or System Board.
The electronic pathways within the computer used to transfer data, memory addresses, and control signals between components.
Carries the actual data between the CPU and memory or peripherals. This bus is bidirectional.
Carries the memory address or specific location of data from the CPU to the memory. This bus is unidirectional.
Carries command signals from the CPU to direct, coordinate, and synchronize the activities of various motherboard components.

sections.title: Major Internal Buses and Slots
sections.description: The main expansion slots and internal interfaces located on the motherboard for connecting internal devices.

key_associations.extra_info: A standard slot previously used for connecting Sound Cards, Modems, and LAN Cards to the motherboard.
The fastest serial bus in modern motherboards, primarily used for connecting advanced Graphics Cards and NVMe Solid State Drives (SSDs).
The primary interface used to connect mass storage devices like Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) and Solid State Drives (SSDs) to the motherboard.
Mainly used in older computers specifically for 3D graphics accelerators. It has now been entirely replaced by PCIe slots.

sections.title: External Ports of Computer
sections.description: Ports located on the back or front panel of the system unit to connect external peripherals.

key_associations.extra_info: Used for connecting keyboards, mice, printers, and pen drives. It also provides electrical power to these external devices.
Transmits high-quality uncompressed video and audio through a single cable to monitors, projectors, or TVs.
A 15-pin, D-sub connector used for older monitors and projectors. It transmits video signals only (no audio).
Used to connect the computer directly to a wired Local Area Network (LAN), router, or high-speed Internet.

sections.title: Legacy Ports and Interfaces
sections.description: Older generation ports that are largely obsolete and rarely used in modern computing systems.

key_associations.extra_info: A 6-pin Mini-DIN connector. Traditionally, the purple port was designated for the keyboard and the green port for the mouse.
A 25-pin port capable of transferring multiple bits of data simultaneously. It was commonly referred to as the Printer Port.
An older 9-pin port that transmitted data sequentially one bit at a time. It was frequently called the COM Port.
Developed by Apple, it was a high-speed data transfer interface primarily used for digital camcorders and external drives.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts and technical details regarding motherboards and buses frequently tested in exams.

important_facts.fact: The CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) is a coin-cell battery on the motherboard that retains system time, date, and BIOS configurations even when the computer is powered off.
USB 3.0 offers a data transfer speed approximately 10 times faster than USB 2.0, and its internal plastic receptacle is typically colored blue to distinguish it.
Thunderbolt is currently one of the fastest external hardware interfaces available, jointly developed by Apple and Intel.
The overall speed and performance of a microprocessor (CPU) depend significantly on the data width and clock speed of the motherboard's Front-Side Bus (FSB).
